entry.title: plugin/bin and the CLI entry — the link, the copy chooser, the verb table and the surface it prints
entry.body:
# The CLI's entry — the link, the copy chooser, the verb table and the surface it prints

The one tree the `module-*` entries of this store did not cover. Read whole at 299f437 during the
ISS-319 batch reading of 44728d4..299f437, which is when `commands.mjs` moved.

## What each file owns

| File | Owns |
|---|---|
| `plugin/bin/forge` | the 17-line link the shell calls |
| `plugin/src/dispatch.mjs` | **which copy of the plugin runs**: `copyToRun({ entry })`, then `argv[1]` set to the real path and the chosen copy imported |
| `plugin/src/cli.mjs` | one verb dispatched: the withholding check, the help routes, `VERB_LIST`/`PREAMBLE`/`MORE`/`FEEDBACK`, and the one `try` around the verb |
| `plugin/src/commands.mjs` | the verb table itself, `export const commands` |
| `plugin/src/suggest.mjs` | `didYouMean`, `unknownFlag` |

## The table has two shapes and nothing states which a verb takes

**13 verbs are one identifier** — `doctor`, `claim`, `resume`, `record`, `advance`, `spec`, `deps`,
`knowledge`, `cloudflare`, `feedback`, `codex`, `hooks`, `stats` — each routing its own sub-verbs
and owning its own refusals in its own module. `knowledge` is five routes and `codex` eight, and
neither costs the table more than a line.

**12 are written inline**: `tools`, `schema`, `call`, `issues`, `issue`, `new`, `comment`, `plan`,
`attach`, `dep`, `guide`, `project`. The two longest are the two that grew routes in
44728d4..299f437 — `guide` at 39 lines and `project` at 47, with a further 40-line `briefRoute`
helper and a four-branch refusal set above the table. Every other function of the brief is in
`plugin/src/tracker/project-config.mjs`; only the decision of which of `--refresh`, `--confirm` and
`--line` a call is asking for lives in the dispatcher. `project` crossed from a two-branch verb into
a four-route one across two releases, so no single diff shows the crossing. Measured onto ISS-322,
which holds this file and adds `forge next` to it.

## Traps read off the code

- **`Object.hasOwn(commands, command)`, never `commands[command]`.** `commands.toString` is
  inherited and callable, so a mistyped verb naming a prototype member ran it and exited 0.
- **A verb's own `-h` is intercepted by `cli.mjs` before the verb sees it**, unless the verb sets
  `answersHelp`. Only `record` and `codex` do. Every other verb read `-h` as a filename, a uuid or a
  tool name before that guard existed. A sub-verb's `-h` is a different question and is still wrong
  in places: ISS-305.
- **The verb list goes to stderr when nothing was asked and to stdout when `-h` was.** `forge -h | head`
  printed nothing before that split, and an answer is not a failure.
- **A withheld verb is refused before its module loads**, by `blockedBy(command)` reading
  `resolve/visibility.mjs`'s `VERBS`. The row's own `refusal` is printed where it has one — that is
  how `forge dep` is withheld on a PAT while `forge deps` keeps reading the same tool.
- **`dispatch.mjs` imports node builtins and the chooser and nothing else, on purpose**: it is the
  thing that survives a broken checkout, and a graph reaching what it survives survives nothing. Its
  fallback names the installed copy by path, and it only prints that where the chosen copy was the
  checkout's — a broken *installed* copy is not a fault in what you typed.
- **`argv[1]` is set to `realpathSync(target)`** before the import, so a main-module guard in the
  target compares against the real path rather than the link.

## The issues that shaped it

ISS-278 gave `VERBS` a per-action gate and a row's own refusal. ISS-295 split the help predicate out
so `plugin/vi-natural/` could spend it without the settings graph. ISS-305 owes the sub-verb help.
ISS-227 owes one unknown-flag reading for every verb, which is today three spellings. ISS-320 is
about to make `plugin/hooks/` choose its copy the way `dispatch.mjs` already does, and holds
`dispatch.mjs` and `plugin/src/tools/plugin-copy.mjs`; ISS-322 holds `commands.mjs` and `cli.mjs`.

Open at 299f437 in this tree: ISS-227, ISS-305, ISS-320, ISS-322, and ISS-114 — `resolve/visibility.mjs`
has four exports read only inside their own file (`knownGates`, `gatedTools`, `withheldVerbs`,
`gateKey`).

## What the ISS-370 reading changed (`8cadbf5..27206a7`)

- **The gate index is walked once per process, not per lookup.** `gateFile` in
  `plugin/src/hooks/hook-switch.mjs` used a `find` over a directory walk; `dispatch` asks per gate of
  an event and `doctor` again per hook, which came to about 20 directory reads on a single tool call.
  It is a `once()`-memoised `Map` now, first-match-wins exactly as the `find` was — a second file of
  one name would be a precedence rule and there is not supposed to be one.
- `forge doctor --full`, `doctor hooks` and `doctor tools --all` print byte for byte what they
  printed before, over 129 lines; that is one of ISS-370's eight differential sections and it is the
  one that exercises this path.
